# Threat model: agentcore-superagent-update

## Overview
Local source assessment of the **AgentCore Demo Platform / Super Agent** multi-agent platform. Product code: `super-agent/backend` (Fastify + Prisma API server, ~67k lines TS), `super-agent/agentcore` (AgentCore Runtime container that executes agent tool calls), `super-agent/frontend` (React), `super-agent/infra` (CDK). All testing was local/offline: no deployed endpoints, no real credentials, no cloud calls. Findings below were validated with local unit harnesses (mocked Prisma / real service code) and harmless marker operations.

Main components:
- `backend/src/routes/*` — Fastify HTTP surface (49 route files; auth, agents, chat, files, skills, MCP, workflows, connectors, LLM proxy).
- `backend/src/services/*` — business logic incl. `claude-agent.service` (spawns Claude CLI agent with hardcoded `bypassPermissions`), `workspace-manager` (git clone plugins, unzip skill archives, S3 download), `dev-server-manager`, `mcp.service`, `agent-runtime-*`.
- `agentcore/src/agent-runner.ts` — agent execution inside the AgentCore runtime container (tool execution, file watcher, workspace sync).
- `backend/src/authorization` + `middleware` — auth, agent/scope access, token quotas.

## Trust Boundaries and Assumptions
- HTTP caller → backend routes: unauthenticated and authenticated users, multi-tenant (organizations, scopes, memberships). Enforcement: `authenticate` on all protected routes, `requireModifyAccess` on writes; object-level org scoping is implemented per-service — **confirmed missing on knowledge-base, briefing, RAG search, userGroups, scopeMemberships, businessScopes plugin/MCP, and support-group routes** (see findings).
- Chat/user prompt → agent runtime → tool execution. **Enforcement confirmed broken on both runtimes**: backend `claude-agent.service` hardcodes `permissionMode: 'bypassPermissions'` with a regex-denylist PreToolUse hook that is trivially bypassed; the AgentCore container runner registers no security hook at all.
- Retrieved content (S3-restored workspaces/skills/CLAUDE.md, RAG documents, web/MCP results) → agent context → tool calls: injection consequence boundary is the broken tool-approval boundary above. LLM-layer injection reachability itself is stochastic and not locally validated (open item).
- Skill/plugin installation: user-controlled `gitUrl`, `ref`, `name`, `localPath` flow unvalidated into `git clone`, path joins, and `cp` — traversal and git argument injection confirmed.
- Files/documents routes use S3-only keys with org-prefix validation; no local-FS write path found there (assessed, no issue).

Actors: anonymous HTTP client, authenticated platform user, tenant admin, the LLM agent (executes with host/container privileges, effectively uncontrolled), and retrieved-content attacker (indirect injection source with confirmed unguarded consequence).

## Attack Surface and Attacker Stories
| Who | Starting access | Path | Result (validated) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Any user prompt / injected content | chat with any agent | unapproved tool call → Bash on backend host | vuln-0006 (critical): marker file created via hook bypass |
| Poisoned workspace/skill/web content | agent run in container | unfiltered Bash/Write/WebFetch + S3 persistence | vuln-0007 (critical) |
| Authenticated user, other tenant | guessed/enumerated KB IDs | read/write/delete other orgs' knowledge bases, folders, files | vuln-0001 (high) |
| Authenticated user | RAG search / index endpoints | cross-org document retrieval and indexing | reported (rag.routes) |
| Scope-admin of own org | businessScopes plugin install | `../`-name traversal + `--upload-pack` git argv injection → command execution | vuln-0003 (high) |
| Authenticated user | skills create / generated skills | out-of-root SKILL.md writes | vuln-0004 (medium) |
| Skill zip source | provisioning with python3 zipfile fallback | zip-slip write outside extraction dir | vuln-0005 (medium) |
| Authenticated user, other tenant | userGroups / scopeMemberships / businessScopes plugin-MCP / support-group member ops | cross-org member removal, role tamper, access-grant rewrite | vuln-0008..0011 (high) |

Unrealistic/out of scope: attacks requiring live AWS (S3, Bedrock, Cognito) — traced statically only per engagement mandate.

## Severity Calibration
Applied: two criticals (broken tool-approval boundary on both runtimes, locally demonstrated with marker operations), six highs (cross-tenant IDOR families; plugin-install traversal + git argv injection), three mediums (bounded traversal, zip-slip, briefing IDOR). Counterevidence and severity-change conditions recorded per report; several route families verified clean and closed as ruled_out / no_issue_found.

Open proof gaps: a2a/openapi/llm-proxy/widget/token-usage/schedules/webhooks/audit/agentPermissions/document-groups handler-level org scoping only spot-checked; RAG prompt-injection reachability at LLM layer not dynamically validated (needs live model).
